title: Ancient Networks in Flux: Environmental Rhythms and Human Connectivity in Arid Landscapes
content: This study investigates how fluctuations in longterm environmental water availability shaped patterns of human interaction and mobility in prehistoric arid regions. Using a combination of geoclimatic reconstructions and archaeological site distributions, we analyze the relationship between climatic stressors and evolving sociocultural connections. The findings reveal dynamic shifts in regional affiliations corresponding with periods of drought and ecological stress, highlighting a strong interplay between hydrological variability and human behavioral adaptation. By examining interaction networks over time, this work offers a novel perspective on how environmental forces influenced communal strategies in ancient societies facing climatic uncertainty.
